land.text: the Avar remnant on the Hungarian plain and the Transylvanian east, taken by Bulgaria 804-806

successors.note: 804: 'Bulgaria conquered the southeastern Avar lands in Transylvania and southeastern Pannonia'; 'Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate'. Bulgaria took the central and eastern Avar lands around 829.

land.text: Pannonia west of the Danube-Tisza line

successors.note: Taken in 796 (Pippin of Italy), nine years before the khaganate's end; 'Pannonia seized by Francia' (infobox).

capitals.name: Khagan's camp on the Pontic steppe (place not named on the pages)
capitals.note: The pages opened name no capital for the steppe years. The point is the centroid of the Cliopatria shape of 561, a placeholder.

capitals.name: The Khagan's court, 'the Ring' (Hungarian plain; place not named on the pages)
capitals.note: The Avar Wars page has a 'ring' sacked in 795/796 but does not place it; the Pannonian Avars infobox gives no capital. The point is the centroid of the Cliopatria shape of 788, a placeholder for the Danube-Tisza heartland; a gap-filler should open the page on the Ring.

keyframe_review.note: 655,633 km2: the lower Danube basin and the Pontic steppe east to about 39E. 'By 562 the Avars controlled the lower Danube basin and the steppes north of the Black Sea'; the embassy to Constantinople is 557 and the 'usual deal' 'winter 558/59', then 'for 20 years to come the Avars, under their Khagan Baian, fought Utigurs and Antes, Gepids and Slavs'. The infobox gives dates ('Established: 567') but no area, so no ratio can be computed.

+97,872 km2 (756,170 km2): 386 of the 387 new cells lie inside Cliopatria's Gepid shape of 565. 'In 567 the Avars formed an alliance with the Lombards-enemies of the Gepids-and together they destroyed much of the Gepid kingdom'; the Gepids page: 'The kingdom is destroyed by the Lombards and Avars: 567'; the Lombards page says the allies split the spoils and the nomads settled in Transylvania.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 569 shape without Sirmium and its 30 km, from spring 568 to 581: 'The city fell in c. 581, or possibly 582.'

keyframe_review.note: +198,526 km2 (959,765 km2): the Lombards' Pannonia and the rest of the Gepid land. Two corrections. The Lombards left in 'the spring of 568' (Lombards page), so the shape should begin in 568, a year before Cliopatria's 569. And the shape contains Sirmium (10 cells within 30 km), which the Avar-Byzantine wars page says fell only 'c. 581, or possibly 582'; until then it is Byzantine (Cliopatria's Eastern Roman shape of 575 does not hold it either).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 577 shape without Sirmium and its 30 km, for 577-581.

keyframe_review.note: 959,317 km2: same land as 569-576. Applies to 577-581 only: Sirmium is Byzantine until 'c. 581, or possibly 582'; from 582 the shape stands unchanged (new keyframe avar-khaganate_582).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 577 shape, applied from 582 to 586 (Sirmium included).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 582-586: the Cliopatria 577 shape unchanged, now with Sirmium. 'By 582, the Avars had captured Sirmium' (Pannonian Avars page) and 'After the capture of Sirmium, the Avars demanded 100,000 solidi a year.' The Danube cities Augustae, Singidunum and Viminacium taken in 583 are not held (Singidunum is besieged and ransomed in 588); the zone is a contest, not Avar land.

959,226 km2: the same land. Maurice's counter-campaigns (Priscus on the Danube in spring 593, Peter's crossing near Securisca in August 594, the Tisza in 601) change no border; 'In 602, the Antes began to invade the Avars' land'. 'By 600 the Avars had established a nomadic empire' stretching 'from modern Austria in the west to the Pontic-Caspian steppe in the east' (Pannonian Avars page, citing a source it flags as unreliable).

+58,420 km2 (1,022,315 km2, the maximum): all 231 new cells lie in Cliopatria's Eastern Roman shape of 600 (16.6-25.1E, 42.6-45.1N). 'The cities of Naissus and Serdica were captured in 615', 'the cities of Novae and Justiniana Prima were destroyed in 613 and 615', Salona fell in the 610s, and 'after 615 the Avars enjoyed a free hand in the undefended Balkans' (Pannonian Avars page). The page gives no area; the 617 shape reaches 13.7E and 39.3E, matching 'from modern Austria ... to the Pontic-Caspian steppe'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 617 shape kept for 623-625: the western Pannonian strip (about 13.7-17.5E) goes to Samo in 626, the Balkan and steppe fringes in 627.

keyframe_review.note: 907,511 km2 against 1,022,315 km2 in 617: Cliopatria takes 444 cells away in 623 (205 into its Samo's Empire shape, 101 back to the Eastern Roman shape, the rest to nobody). No page opened records a loss before 626: the Avars attack Heraclius in 617, meet him in Thrace in 623 and besiege Constantinople in 626, and 'After failing to capture Constantinople, the Avars rapidly began to decline'. Samo is a Frankish merchant who 'went to the Slavs in c. 623-624' (the Samo page questions the date) and the Pannonian Avars infobox has 'Defeated by Samo: 626'. The 617 shape therefore stands through 625.

correction.text: The 617 shape without the western Pannonian strip (205 cells, 13.7-17.5E, 45.5-48.3N) that Samo's union holds from the 626 defeat; Thrace before Constantinople is the 626 contest zone, not Avar land.

keyframe_review.note: 926,825 km2: the 623 shape plus 69 cells (17,450 km2) of Thrace and the Black Sea coast west of Constantinople, the Avar camp of the siege that began on '29 June 626'. Corrected: the 617 shape minus the strip that Samo's revolt takes ('Defeated by Samo: 626'; 'Samo definitively took strategic advantage of the Avar defeat in 626'); the Thracian cells are a contested zone (June-August 626), not Avar land: 'On August 7 ... the Avar land assaults ... were repelled' and the Avars retreated within two days.

828,444 km2: 361 cells lost in 627 (75 of them to the Eastern Roman shape of 627, two to Samo, the rest to no polity). 'After failing to capture Constantinople, the Avars rapidly began to decline before disintegrating entirely' (Avar-Byzantine wars page); infobox 'Conquered by White Croats in Dalmatia: 620s-630s'. Kept as drawn; the ledger carries the 627 losses against the corrected 626 shape.
828,910 km2: one cell added; no event on the pages.
828,397 km2: three cells swapped; no event on the pages.

729,130 km2: 409 cells (103,436 km2, 32.0-39.2E, 46.1-50.4N) go to Cliopatria's Old Great Bulgaria shape of 633. 'Between 630 and 635, Khan Kubrat managed to unite the Onogur Bulgars' and 'overthrow Avar domination' (infobox reign 632-665). The page puts Great Bulgaria 'between the Dniester and lower Volga', which sits uneasily with an Avar shape that keeps Ukraine west of 32E to 655; unresolved, see notes.
729,038 km2: a four-cell swap on the Danube (22.8-23.6E and 25.3-26.9E); no event on the pages.

268,428 km2: 1,859 cells (470,141 km2) drop out in 656, 226 of them into Old Great Bulgaria's enlarged shape (to 301,064 km2) and the other 1,633 (Ukraine, Moldova and Romanian Moldavia, 22.6-37.8E) into no polity. 'In the mid-7th century, Great Bulgaria expanded west to include Avar territory'; it 'disintegrated under Khazar pressure in 668'. The 656 year is Cliopatria's; the page says only 'mid-7th century' (unverified).
+13,151 km2 (282,820 km2): 52 cells at 16.2-21.0E, 45.1-48.1N, 20 of them inside Samo's shape of 658. 'With the death of Samo in 658 and Kubrat in 665, some Slavic tribes again came under Avar rule.'
283,030 km2: one cell added; no event on the pages.

238,606 km2: 195 cells lost north of the lower Danube (22.5-27.9E, 43.6-45.5N, 177 of them inside the First Bulgarian Empire's 682 shape) and an exclave of 28 cells gained in Macedonia (21.5-22.9E, 41.1-42.2N). The Avar-Byzantine wars page: the Avar land 'was further reduced by the Bulgars around 680'. The First Bulgarian Empire page: Kuber's Bulgars 'initially settled in Pannonia under Avar suzerainty but revolted and moved to the region of Macedonia' (undated), which may be the exclave; a revolted group is not Avar land, so the exclave is doubtful; kept as drawn (unverified, see notes).

254,514 km2: +93 cells in Slavonia and the Sava-Drava interfluve (15.3-18.9E, 44.9-46.4N), lying in no other polity's shape, and -28 cells of the Macedonian exclave. The pages opened are silent on both (unverified: page silent).

254,604 km2: unchanged but for three cells. 'By around 700, the course of the river Enns formed the khaganate's frontier with Bavaria', close to the shape's western edge at 15.2E (the Enns lies at about 14.5E).
254,514 km2: the western limit lies at the Enns. 'According to Einhard's account, the war started in 788'; the Avars 'attacked northern Italy and Bavaria, but both armies were defeated'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 788 shape kept for 793-795: the Avars still hold Pannonia; the Frankish gain is dated 796 (new keyframe avar-khaganate_796).

keyframe_review.note: 145,973 km2: 415 cells (104,954 km2; Transdanubia, Slavonia and Burgenland, 15.4-21.0E, 44.8-48.0N) pass to Cliopatria's Frankish shape of 793. The pages date no Frankish gain in 793: Charlemagne's 791 campaign 'reaching as far as the river Rába' was abandoned 'in the middle of October' and Pippin's campaign that 'forced the khagan to submit himself to the Franks' is 796. The 788 shape therefore stands for 793-795.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 793 shape, applied from 796 to 799 (the Franks hold Pannonia west of the Danube-Tisza line).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 796-799: Cliopatria's 793 shape (Pannonia west of the Danube-Tisza line lost). 'Pippin of Italy and Eric of Friuli gathered troops for a new invasion of the Avar Khaganate in 796' and 'forced the khagan to submit himself to the Franks'; infobox 'Pannonia seized by Francia'; 'The Avars who refused the khagan's reconciliatory policy withdrew to the lands to the east of the Tisza.'
177,736 km2: 121 cells regained between the Danube and the Tisza (18.9-21.0E, 44.8-47.9N). 'In 799, some Avars revolted'. Applies to 800-803; from 804 see avar-khaganate_804.

correction.text: The 800 shape without Transylvania and the Banat, conquered by Bulgaria in 804 (southeastern Pannonia read as the Banat).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 804-805: the 800 shape without Transylvania and the south-east. 'In 804, Bulgaria conquered the southeastern Avar lands in Transylvania and southeastern Pannonia'; the First Bulgarian Empire page: 'Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate'. 'Southeastern Pannonia' is not named more closely, so the Banat stands in for it (the broad Transylvania region includes Crisana and the Banat).

region.text: the lower Danube basin and the steppes north of the Black Sea

ledger.note: 561: the Avars, who reached Europe in 557-559 from the Caucasus steppe, hold the lower Danube and the Pontic steppe under Khagan Baian. 'By 562 the Avars controlled the lower Danube basin and the steppes north of the Black Sea'; the infobox has 'Established: 567'. The year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Gepid heartland east of the Tisza, Transylvania and the Banat

ledger.note: 567: the Avars and Lombards destroy the Gepid kingdom. 'In 567 the Avars formed an alliance with the Lombards-enemies of the Gepids-and together they destroyed much of the Gepid kingdom.' Gepids page: 'The kingdom is destroyed by the Lombards and Avars: 567'; the Lombards page says the allies split the spoils and the nomads settled in Transylvania. The land is the Cliopatria diff (386 of 387 cells in the Gepid shape).

region.text: Pannonia and the rest of the Gepid land, left by the Lombards (without Sirmium, Byzantine until c. 581/582)

ledger.note: 568: the Lombards leave Pannonia for Italy and the Avars take it over. 'In the spring of 568, Alboin, now fearing the aggressive Avars, led the Lombard migration into Italy'; 'The Avars have agreed to shelter them if they wish to come back.' The page does not say the Avars took the land; the region is the Cliopatria diff, which begins in 569. [Reviewer eu-06-f, 2026-10-20: Sirmium removed from the region, as in the 569/577 corrections: 'The city fell in c. 581, or possibly 582.']

region.text: Sirmium, the former Roman capital in Pannonia

ledger.note: 582: the Avars capture Sirmium. 'The city fell in c. 581, or possibly 582.' and, on the Pannonian Avars page, 'By 582, the Avars had captured Sirmium'; 'After the capture of Sirmium, the Avars demanded 100,000 solidi a year.'

region.text: the Danube cities Singidunum, Viminacium and Augustae

ledger.note: 583: the Avars take the Danube cities. 'The Avars took the cities of Augustae, Singidunum, and Viminacium in 583, and a further eight cities by siege in 586'; in 588 they 'abandoned the siege of Singidunum after only seven days'. No lasting border change; Maurice's counter-campaigns follow (593-601).

region.text: the Danube frontier from Singidunum to Viminacium

ledger.note: 602: the Balkan war of Maurice's reign ends. 'Maurice was overthrown in 602 by Phocas, as his army rebelled against endless Balkan campaigning'; the Avars 'did not attack Byzantine territory until c. 615'. The Antes invade the Avar land the same year.

region.text: Naissus, Serdica and the Balkan interior, taken in 613-615

ledger.note: 615: the Avars take the Balkan interior. 'The cities of Naissus and Serdica were captured in 615'; 'Novae and Justiniana Prima were destroyed in 613 and 615'; Salona fell in the 610s. The region is the Cliopatria diff of 617 (all 231 cells in the Eastern Roman shape of 600).

region.text: the western Pannonian strip between about 13.7E and 17.5E that passes to Samo's union

ledger.note: 626: the Slavs under Samo break away from the Avars. Infobox 'Defeated by Samo: 626'; Samo page: he 'definitively took strategic advantage of the Avar defeat in 626' and gained a 'string of victories over the Avars'. Cliopatria draws Samo's Empire from 623; the Samo page dates his arrival 'c. 623-624' and his realm 631-658. The land is the Cliopatria diff (205 cells).

region.text: Thrace and the coast west of Constantinople, the Avar camp of the siege

ledger.note: June 626: the Avars and Persians besiege Constantinople. 'On 29 June 626, the Avars and Persians began a coordinated assault upon the walls.' The zone is the Cliopatria diff of 626 (69 cells).

region.text: Thrace and the coast west of Constantinople

ledger.note: August 626: the siege fails. 'The Avar land assaults on August 6 and 7 were repelled' and the Avars retreated within two days: 'They would never seriously threaten Constantinople again.'

region.text: Thrace and the Balkan fringe returned to the empire

ledger.note: 627: after Constantinople the Avar hold on the Balkans collapses. 'After failing to capture Constantinople, the Avars rapidly began to decline before disintegrating entirely.' 103 cells lie in the Eastern Roman shape of 627. [Reviewer eu-06-f, 2026-10-20: confidence 1: the Avar-Byzantine wars page gives no 627 and no Roman recovery; 99 of the 103 cells are the Naissus-Serdica interior that the eastern-roman-empire dossier keeps out of its 623-625 shape ('no page returns them').]

region.text: the Balkan interior and the Dalmatian hinterland, lost to Slavic, Croat and Serb tribes

ledger.note: 627: the Slavic tribes of the Balkans leave Avar rule. Infobox 'Conquered by White Croats in Dalmatia: 620s-630s'. The land is the Cliopatria diff; no polity of the Croats or Serbs has a Cliopatria row, so the counterpart is nobody.

region.text: the steppe between the Dnieper and the Donets

ledger.note: c. 633: Kubrat's Onogur Bulgars shake off Avar rule. 'Between 630 and 635, Khan Kubrat managed to unite the Onogur Bulgars' and 'quickly managed to overthrow Avar domination'; infobox reign 632-665. 409 cells, all in Old Great Bulgaria's shape of 633.

region.text: the western steppe added to Great Bulgaria in the mid-7th century

ledger.note: 656: Great Bulgaria widens into Avar land. 'In the mid-7th century, Great Bulgaria expanded west to include Avar territory.' 226 cells; the year is Cliopatria's. [Reviewer eu-06-f, 2026-10-20: confidence 1: the page gives 'In the mid-7th century', no year.]

region.text: Ukraine, Moldova and Romanian Moldavia, 22.6-37.8E

ledger.note: 656: the Avar claim on the Dniester-Dnieper steppe lapses (Cliopatria; 1,633 cells, 413,000 km2). The Old Great Bulgaria page says the state was 'originally centered between the Dniester and lower Volga' and that 'Kotrag, the leader of the Kutrigurs, took control of the western steppe' (undated); it dates nothing in 656. Bridging judgement.

region.text: Slavic tribes of western Pannonia, returned to Avar rule after Samo

ledger.note: c. 661: part of Samo's former union returns to the Avars. 'With the death of Samo in 658 and Kubrat in 665, some Slavic tribes again came under Avar rule.' 52 cells, 20 of them in Samo's shape of 658; the year is Cliopatria's. [Reviewer eu-06-f, 2026-10-20: confidence 1: the page dates no return of the Slavs to Avar rule; 661 is Cliopatria's.]

region.text: the lower Danube lands north of the river, settled by Asparukh's Bulgars

ledger.note: c. 680: Asparukh's Bulgars settle north and south of the lower Danube. The Avar land 'was further reduced by the Bulgars around 680'; the Pannonian Avars page has 'The Danube settlement (c. 679-681), establishing the First Bulgarian Empire'; the First Bulgarian Empire page: 'In 681, the Byzantines were compelled to sign a humiliating peace treaty, forcing them to acknowledge Bulgaria as an independent state.' 177 cells; Cliopatria's shape is dated 682.

region.text: Slavonia and the Sava-Drava interfluve

ledger.note: 741: Cliopatria adds Slavonia (93 cells, 23,500 km2) to the shape and removes the Macedonian exclave. The Pannonian Avars page is silent on both: bridging judgement.

region.text: the Danube corridor from the Enns to the Raba

ledger.note: Summer 791: Charlemagne invades the khaganate. 'In the summer of 791, after unsuccessful peace negotiations, Charlemagne invaded the khaganate'; the Franks destroy two fortresses across the Enns, the Avars abandon those at the Kamp, and the army reaches 'the river Raba'.

region.text: the Danube corridor from the Enns to the Raba

ledger.note: October 791: the Franks withdraw. 'A pestilence broke out in Charlemagne's camp killing about 90% of their horses' and he 'was to abandon the campaign in the middle of October.'

region.text: Pannonia west of the Danube-Tisza line: Transdanubia, Slavonia, Burgenland

ledger.note: 796: Pippin of Italy takes Pannonia. 'Pippin of Italy and Eric of Friuli gathered troops for a new invasion of the Avar Khaganate in 796' and 'forced the khagan to submit himself to the Franks without resistance'; infobox 'Pannonia seized by Francia'. Cliopatria dates the Frankish gain 793; the pages give 796. 415 cells.

region.text: the Danube-Tisza interfluve, back under Avar rule

ledger.note: 800: the central Hungarian plain returns to the Avars in Cliopatria (121 cells). 'In 799, some Avars revolted'; the pages say nothing more. Bridging judgement.

region.text: the southeastern Avar lands in Transylvania and southeastern Pannonia

ledger.note: 804: Khan Krum's Bulgaria takes Transylvania. 'In 804, Bulgaria conquered the southeastern Avar lands in Transylvania and southeastern Pannonia'; the First Bulgarian Empire page: 'Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate'. 'Southeastern Pannonia' is read as the Banat.

region.text: the Avar remnant on the Hungarian plain, divided between the Franks and Bulgaria

ledger.note: 805: the Avar Khaganate ends. 'Khagan Theodorus, a convert to Christianity, died after asking Charlemagne for help in 805'; Bulgaria 'expanded its territory northwest to the Pannonian Plain' (First Bulgarian Empire page) and, around 829, took 'the central and eastern portions of traditional Avar lands'; the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 822' and the last Avar prince is mentioned in 822.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid War

zones.text: the Gepid kingdom between the Tisza, the Carpathians and the Sava

wars.outcome: The Avars and Lombards 'destroyed much of the Gepid kingdom' in 567; the Avars took the east and, after the Lombards left in 568, the rest.
wars.note: Gepids page: 'The Gepids were finally overrun by the Avars in the 567 Lombard-Gepid war.' Treaty terms are not on the pages.

wars.name: Avar siege and capture of Sirmium
wars.outcome: 'The city fell in c. 581, or possibly 582'; the Avars then demanded 100,000 solidi a year.
wars.note: The page gives only 'c. 581, or possibly 582' for the fall; no start of the siege is dated.

wars.name: Avar-Byzantine Balkan war of Maurice's reign

zones.text: the Danube frontier at Singidunum and Viminacium

wars.outcome: Avar captures on the Danube (583, 586), a ransomed siege of Singidunum (588), Byzantine crossings under Priscus (593, 599) and Peter (594, 601); no lasting border change. Ended with Maurice's fall in 602.
wars.note: Tomis was besieged until 30 March 598; the Antes invaded the Avar land in 602.

wars.name: Avar-Byzantine war of Heraclius' reign
wars.outcome: The Avars took Naissus and Serdica (615), besieged Thessalonica (617) and, with the Persians, besieged Constantinople from 29 June 626; the assaults of 6-7 August were repelled and they retreated.
wars.note: 'They would never seriously threaten Constantinople again.'

wars.name: Samo's rebellion against the Avars
wars.outcome: Samo's 'string of victories over the Avars' made him king and split the western Slavs from the Avars; in 631 or 632 he also beat Dagobert I's Franks.
wars.note: The page questions Fredegar's c. 623-624 date for Samo's arrival; 'during Samo's rebellion in 631, 9,000 Bulgars led by Alciocus left Pannonia' (Pannonian Avars page).

wars.name: Kubrat's revolt
wars.outcome: Kubrat united the Onogur Bulgars and 'overthrew Avar domination' between 630 and 635.
wars.note: The Pannonian Avars page puts the uprising 'at about the time of Samo's realm'.

wars.name: Bulgar settlement on the lower Danube

zones.text: the lower Danube lands north of the river

wars.outcome: The Avar land 'was further reduced by the Bulgars around 680'; Byzantium recognised Bulgaria in 681.
wars.note: The Avars are not named as a combatant on the pages opened; the war was Asparukh's against Constantine IV (Onglos 680).

wars.name: Charlemagne's Avar War

zones.text: Pannonia west of the Danube-Tisza line

wars.outcome: Avar attacks on Bavaria and Italy failed in 788; Charlemagne reached the Raba in 791; Pippin of Italy and Eric of Friuli made the khagan submit in 796 and the Franks seized Pannonia; the Avars who refused withdrew east of the Tisza.
wars.note: The Avar-Byzantine wars page dates the Frankish conquest 'starting in 790 and ending in 803'; the 799 revolt, the 803 submission of the tudun and the 805 baptism of Theodorus are not on the Avar Wars page. [Reviewer eu-06-f, 2026-10-20: to 803 from the Avar Wars infobox, 'Date: 788 to 803'.]

wars.name: Bulgarian conquest of the Avar east
wars.outcome: 'Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate'; a border with the Frankish Empire was established along the middle Danube or the Tisza.
wars.note: The page adds that Krum was 'occupying the vast lands along the middle Danube'.

certainty.note: Steppe and plain frontiers throughout. The Danube line against Byzantium and the Enns against Bavaria ('By around 700, the course of the river Enns formed the khaganate's frontier with Bavaria') are river lines but untreated; no treaty with a surveyed border is on the pages opened.

notes:
Avar Khaganate, 561-805 (22 Cliopatria shapes, 8 pages).
- Start/end: Cliopatria 561..805; the page says the Avars arrived in 557-559, 'Established: 567', 'Disestablished: 822'. The state is kept at 561..805 (control of the lower Danube by 562; Theodorus died 805; Bulgaria 804-806).
- Cliopatria 617-626: the shape drops 444 cells in 623 (Samo, Eastern Roman, nobody) although the pages show a strong Avar state until 626 and a collapse after it. Verdicts 623 and 626 adjust: keep the 617 shape to 625, take Samo's strip in 626, the rest in 627. The Samo dossier (eu-15) draws Samo's Empire from 623 (Cliopatria) and the page gives 'c. 623-624' for his arrival and 631-658 for the realm; the two dossiers overlap for 623-625 and need reconciling.
- Cliopatria 569-581 holds Sirmium, which fell c. 581/582: corrections for 569/577 and a new keyframe 582.
- Cliopatria 793 gives the Frankish gain three years before the pages (796): corrected with a new keyframe 796.
- Doubts left open: (1) the Avar shape keeps the Dniester-Dnieper steppe to 655 but the OGB page puts Great Bulgaria 'between the Dniester and lower Volga' from 632; (2) the 28-cell Macedonian exclave of 682-740 may be Kuber's revolted Bulgars; (3) the 741 gain of Slavonia and the 800 return of the Danube-Tisza interfluve are Cliopatria-only (confidence 1).
- Capitals: no page names the khagan's seat; both entries are centroids of Cliopatria shapes, placeholders flagged in their notes.
